sparse_decode.interpretation: scale hoisting materially improved INT4, but production INT4 sparse decode remains about 23-25% slower than byte-FP8 and is currently a memory-capacity candidate rather than a decode-speed candidate

untested_or_unaccepted_risks: No full DeepSeek-V4 server/model-weight launch was performed for this receipt.
No end-to-end dual-GPU throughput, TTFT, concurrency, OpenCode, or coherency run was performed; the observed NV4 topology alone does not prove active NVLink traffic in a model run.
Plain symmetric per-64 latent INT4 is outlier-sensitive and has not passed long-context quality/coherency acceptance. It can perturb QK top-k selection and PV output more than byte-FP8.
The C4 indexer path is lower risk because its existing normalized H128 rotation precedes per-32 INT4 scoring, but it still requires full-model selection-recall and coherency validation.

An H64 latent rotation would preserve QK only if applied to both Q and K; because DeepSeek-V4 shares K/V, PV output would remain in the rotated basis unless an inverse is fused or exactly absorbed into wo_a. H64/H32 rotation is therefore not enabled.
OSCAR-style learned rotations require calibration data and acceptance testing and are not enabled.

INT4 sparse decode is slower than the Ampere byte-FP8 path in isolated production-shape microbenchmarks; promotion should be based on memory headroom enabling a better whole-model configuration, not an assumed kernel speedup.
disposition: complete, CUDA-graph-safe SM86 implementation; hold behind opt-in flags as a memory-capacity candidate until full-server coherency and long-context quality gates pass
